memory_update.text: Highest-confidence direct equipment names for data_center_power_cooling_and_grid: VRT, ETN, GEV, TT, JCI, CARR.
Grid construction and labor chokepoint mapping should include PWR and FIX; both need deeper backlog/revenue-mix validation before ranking.
Power-generation and regulated-asset mapping should include CEG, VST and NEE; thesis quality depends on PPA terms, regional power markets, ratepayer/regulatory treatment and project execution.

Distribution and component layer should include HUBB and WCC; these are second-order suppliers where evidence should focus on data-center sales mix, utility T&D backlog, scarce components and margin capture.
DLR is included as a customer/owner of constrained data-center capacity rather than a supplier; power-secured land and available IT capacity are the key evidence variables.

Potential additional names not included due to 15-candidate cap: EQIX, AES, APLD, IREN, ATKR, GNRC, BWXT, LEU, SMR, ABBNY, SBGSY, SIEGY, KMI, BKR, APH, FLEX, NVT, BDC and DY. Consider separate Layer 1B expansions for nuclear fuel/SMR, data-center REITs/neoclouds, electrical components, and gas/pipeline/on-site generation.

Primary chokepoint variables to track across this node: secured MW/GW of power, grid interconnection timelines, transformer/switchgear lead times, liquid-cooling adoption, thermal-management performance, construction labor, data-center backlog, hyperscaler concentration and regional regulatory/power-price pressure.

node: Data-center power, liquid cooling, electrical gear, and grid infrastructure
summary: Expanded US-listed universe for the AI data-center power/cooling/grid node. The strongest direct exposures cluster in critical digital infrastructure, electrical equipment, grid construction, commercial mechanical/electrical contracting, thermal management, on-site generation, power generation, utilities, data-center REITs, and electrical distribution. This is a research universe, not a recommendation list. Candidate inclusion reflects plausible chokepoint exposure; company-level revenue mix, backlog quality, margins, customer concentration, and regulatory/power-price risks still require deeper Layer 2 evidence.
